questions.question: What is the energy difference between the staggered and eclipsed conformations of ethane?

options.label: A
options.text: The eclipsed conformation is 12 kJ/mol (2.9 kcal/mol) higher in potential energy due to torsional strain between adjacent C-H bonds.

options.label: B
options.text: The eclipsed conformation is 100 kJ/mol more stable.

options.label: C
options.text: The staggered conformation is 50 kJ/mol higher in energy.

options.label: D
options.text: Both conformations have identical potential energy.

questions.correct_answer: The eclipsed conformation is 12 kJ/mol (2.9 kcal/mol) higher in potential energy due to torsional strain between adjacent C-H bonds.
questions.explanation: Three pairs of eclipsed C-H bonds create 3 × 4.0 kJ/mol = 12 kJ/mol of torsional strain.

questions.question: Rank the four principal conformations of n-butane in order of increasing potential energy:

options.label: A
options.text: Anti (0 kJ/mol) < Gauche (3.8 kJ/mol) < Eclipsed H/CH₃ (16 kJ/mol) < Fully Eclipsed CH₃/CH₃ (19 kJ/mol).

options.label: B
options.text: Fully Eclipsed < Eclipsed < Gauche < Anti.

options.label: C
options.text: All conformations have identical energy.

options.label: D
options.text: Gauche < Anti < Fully Eclipsed < Eclipsed.

questions.correct_answer: Anti (0 kJ/mol) < Gauche (3.8 kJ/mol) < Eclipsed H/CH₃ (16 kJ/mol) < Fully Eclipsed CH₃/CH₃ (19 kJ/mol).
questions.explanation: Anti is the global minimum; gauche experiences steric strain (3.8 kJ/mol); fully eclipsed has maximum steric and torsional strain (19 kJ/mol).

questions.question: Rank the following cycloalkanes in order of increasing total ring strain: cyclohexane, cyclopentane, cyclobutane, cyclopropane.

options.label: A
options.text: Cyclopropane < Cyclobutane < Cyclopentane < Cyclohexane.

options.label: B
options.text: Cyclopentane has zero ring strain.

options.label: C
options.text: All cycloalkanes have identical ring strain.

options.label: D
options.text: Cyclohexane (0 kJ/mol) < Cyclopentane (27 kJ/mol) < Cyclobutane (110 kJ/mol) < Cyclopropane (115 kJ/mol).

questions.correct_answer: Cyclohexane (0 kJ/mol) < Cyclopentane (27 kJ/mol) < Cyclobutane (110 kJ/mol) < Cyclopropane (115 kJ/mol).
questions.explanation: Cyclohexane is completely strain-free; cyclopropane and cyclobutane suffer severe angle and torsional strain.

questions.question: What geometric features make the chair conformation of cyclohexane completely strain-free?

options.label: A
options.text: All hydrogens occupy axial positions simultaneously.

options.label: B
options.text: The ring is a completely flat planar hexagon.

options.label: C
options.text: The ring contains three double bonds.

options.label: D
options.text: All C-C-C bond angles are 109.5° (zero angle strain) and all adjacent C-H bonds are fully staggered (zero torsional strain).

questions.correct_answer: All C-C-C bond angles are 109.5° (zero angle strain) and all adjacent C-H bonds are fully staggered (zero torsional strain).
questions.explanation: The chair conformation achieves perfect tetrahedral angles (109.5°) and fully staggered dihedral angles around all 6 C-C bonds.

questions.question: In methylcyclohexane, what percentage of molecules exist in the equatorial conformation at 25°C?

options.label: A
options.text: 10% equatorial / 90% axial.

options.label: B
options.text: 50% equatorial / 50% axial.

options.label: C
options.text: 100% axial.

options.label: D
options.text: Approximately 95% equatorial (A-value = 7.3 kJ/mol), because the equatorial conformer avoids 1,3-diaxial steric interactions.

questions.correct_answer: Approximately 95% equatorial (A-value = 7.3 kJ/mol), because the equatorial conformer avoids 1,3-diaxial steric interactions.
questions.explanation: An equatorial methyl group avoids two 1,3-diaxial gauche interactions (~7.3 kJ/mol), placing 95% of molecules in the equatorial chair at 25°C.

questions.question: Why is the tert-butyl group considered a 'conformational locking group' on cyclohexane rings?

options.label: A
options.text: tert-Butyl forms covalent bonds with the ring carbons.

options.label: B
options.text: tert-Butyl group is always axial.

options.label: C
options.text: tert-Butyl forces the ring into a planar hexagon.

options.label: D
options.text: Its enormous A-value (~20 kJ/mol) dictates that >99.9% of molecules adopt the chair conformation with the tert-butyl group in the equatorial position.

questions.correct_answer: Its enormous A-value (~20 kJ/mol) dictates that >99.9% of molecules adopt the chair conformation with the tert-butyl group in the equatorial position.
questions.explanation: Severe 1,3-diaxial steric clash locks the bulky tert-butyl group in the equatorial position (>99.99% at equilibrium).

questions.question: What is the conformational relationship between the two chair forms of cis-1,4-dimethylcyclohexane upon chair flipping?

options.label: A
options.text: One chair is a planar hexagon.

options.label: B
options.text: One chair is 50 kJ/mol more stable.

options.label: C
options.text: Both chair conformations are degenerate (identical in energy), each having exactly one axial methyl and one equatorial methyl group (a,e ⇌ e,a).

options.label: D
options.text: One chair has both methyls equatorial (e,e) and the other has both axial (a,a).

questions.correct_answer: Both chair conformations are degenerate (identical in energy), each having exactly one axial methyl and one equatorial methyl group (a,e ⇌ e,a).
questions.explanation: A chair flip of cis-1,4-dimethylcyclohexane interconverts an (axial, equatorial) chair into an identical (equatorial, axial) chair.

questions.question: What is the conformational relationship between the two chair forms of trans-1,4-dimethylcyclohexane upon chair flipping?

options.label: A
options.text: One chair conformation is diequatorial (e,e - highly stable) and the flipped chair is diaxial (a,a - high energy, destabilized by 15 kJ/mol).

options.label: B
options.text: Both chair forms are degenerate (a,e ⇌ e,a).

options.label: C
options.text: The diaxial conformer is more stable than the diequatorial conformer.

options.label: D
options.text: The molecule exists exclusively in a boat conformation.

questions.correct_answer: One chair conformation is diequatorial (e,e - highly stable) and the flipped chair is diaxial (a,a - high energy, destabilized by 15 kJ/mol).
questions.explanation: In trans-1,4-dimethylcyclohexane, the diequatorial conformer (e,e) is favored over the diaxial conformer (a,a) by ~15 kJ/mol (>99% population).

questions.question: Why is cis-1,3-dimethylcyclohexane overwhelmingly more stable in its (e,e) chair conformation than trans-1,3-dimethylcyclohexane?

options.label: A
options.text: The cis isomer contains an internal triple bond.

options.label: B
options.text: The cis isomer has a lower molecular weight.

options.label: C
options.text: The cis isomer can place BOTH methyl groups in equatorial positions (e,e), whereas the trans isomer is forced to have one axial and one equatorial group (a,e).

options.label: D
options.text: The trans isomer is an antiaromatic ring.

questions.correct_answer: The cis isomer can place BOTH methyl groups in equatorial positions (e,e), whereas the trans isomer is forced to have one axial and one equatorial group (a,e).
questions.explanation: cis-1,3-Dimethylcyclohexane achieves a strain-free diequatorial (e,e) chair, whereas the trans-1,3 isomer is locked in an (a,e) state.
